utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The Court will see this morning there is a third amicus in court. That is Professor McCormack from Australia, who was appointed by the order of the Trial Chamber to assist on matters of international law, and he is present this week for the hearings and to deal with any issues the Trial Chamber may ask of him. Perhaps he can introduce himself to the Trial Chamber now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. McCormack, let me say we've got an application which you've made for an extension of time for the preparation of submissions. You asked for an extension of the same period of time as we initially allowed, your not having had the papers or anything to work on it. We'll certainly grant that until the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCORMACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I'm sorry that I have to ask for that extension of time for such a long time, but as all three of you know, the process of me actually being able to commence my work has taken a little bit longer than I hoped it would but I'm very pleased to be here today. Thanks for the welcome, and looking forward to working with you on the aspects of the trial that you've designated me to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCORMACK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll deal next with the witness. Mr. Gusalic, I understand occasionally you may need a break when giving evidence. If you do, if you want a break, just tell us and you can have one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Nice: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, before we return to where we were at the end of yesterday, you told us about Mauzer's men and about Mauzer. Do you remember now of which brigade Mauzer had originally been a member?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the Panthers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he himself, do you know what he had done by way of military service before having this group which you now connect in some way to the name Panthers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 5 of the summary, paragraph 18. Mr. Gusalic, you told us of your first experiences in the hospital and of the visit by Blagojevic with two of his men. Were you and others in the hospital visited later by other well-known individuals? If so, tell us by whom.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was visited by Mrs. Plavsic, Fikret Abdic, Arkan also came, and Mirko Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those first three or four people, did they come just to see you or did they come to see many people in the hospital; and if so, with what message?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just me. They toured the whole hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was said, for example, by Arkan?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arkan didn't say anything in particular, but Mrs. Plavsic said that this had all been done by the paramilitary, that the Yugoslav People's Army would deal with it and calm things down. And later on, it did calm things down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were orders given as to whether you should be treated or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I stayed there for only nine days and I was released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, just one moment. We're not getting our transcripts running. All we've got is the first part of the morning's work. Yes, apparently it will be sorted out. Provided we're keeping a transcript, all well and good. Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in fact treated by hospital staff, Mr. Gusalic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was for the first three days, but later, they would hit me, and after the visit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Apparently there is a problem with the transcript and we'll need to break for five minutes. We'll adjourn for five minutes for that to be done. --- Break taken at 9.16 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, when you were released from hospital, did you go home?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Arkan at the time of your release from hospital or at about that time? If so, did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the hospital when Mrs. Plavsic and Fikret Abdic came, but after that, I didn't see him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to go home? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arkan personally released me, and he said that I should go home and that no one would hurt me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything further about whether you should go home and stay at home or whether you were free to roam around, or what?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I should go home and stay there, not leave home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a small bundle of exhibits for this witness, three altogether, and indeed as I've already indicated I'm not going to produce the second, but may they, for convenience, be given an exhibit number with two tab references in the event.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecutor's Exhibit 414.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And of Exhibit 414, tab 1 is a photograph now on your -- it's not now on the witness's screen. May it be displayed for the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise one or both of the men in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise only one. That is Arkan, the one on the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following your release from prison -- and, Your Honour, I'm going to try and deal with pages 5 and 6 fairly briefly, I think. Following your release from prison -- from hospital, did you receive letters of a threatening kind?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive letters. Who sent them, I don't know for sure, but they were threatening letters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you visited by men from identified groups?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were soldiers coming all the time to my house, as if it was a garrison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do to you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't do anything. They just cursed my balija mother, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you arrested on two occasions in this period of time following your release from hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or had you started the process of hiding at the time of your first arrest, hiding from the men who were visiting you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got that last letter, I got scared, and then I started to escape, and they were looking for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think they found you and they took you to the SUP building in Bijeljina; correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, when they found you, they forced you to surrender by saying something over a loudspeaker about what would happen to your wife, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and to my whole family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they say would happen to your family if you didn't give yourself up?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they would all be killed if I didn't surrender. So I decided it was better for me alone than my whole family to suffer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the local SUP building, what treatment did you receive from the police?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't talk much. They just hit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you handcuffed at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was something said to you about the treatment you were receiving and the way it's different from the way you would have been treated had you been detained by Blagojevic's men?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was certainly better that I was captured by the police than by Mirko's men, because if they had caught me on the very first occasion, they would have killed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was something said to you or something you calculated yourself?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I calculated that myself. No one told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you needed to go to the toilet and you asked to have the handcuffs taken off?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you were released from the handcuffs, what were you able to do?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no choice; I hit the policeman and ran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you escaped?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then hid for about 20 days in a cemetery and in some woods?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that. Around 20 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later, you felt you had to go back and see your wife who'd recently given birth to a new baby?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a daughter. She was a month and a half old, and I decided to go and see her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At your house, were you arrested again?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men came to arrest you? Did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On their heads?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black scarves -- no, socks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise -- think again, please. Did you recognise any one of those men?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently discover whether your wife, your brother, and your child had been treated in any way to force them to reveal your presence at the house?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, before that, my wife, brother, and my baby daughter, while I was escaping, they took them to the barracks. They put them in some sort of a freezer for them to confess where I was hiding, though no one knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this second arrest, were you taken to the local SUP building?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days were you kept there, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not roughly; for four days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided with wood or water over those four days?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was just provided with beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did the beatings?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who didn't. Whoever came in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the police commander at the time? What was his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this witness is obviously having some difficulty yesterday and today remembering matters of detail. Giving evidence is always a stressful experience. I propose to ask him if he's recorded these matters in his statement and, subject to objection, I'll put a name to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you record at an earlier time the name of the police commander and, I think, put it in a witness statement? I'll just check that it's in the witness statement rather than in the proofing notes. Did you? Did you put the name of the police commander in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mica, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mica, had he formed a special unit of men as well as being a general police commander?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander. Yes, he did. He had his special men. Perhaps 30 or 35 men, young men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those some of the men who came and beat you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All 30 of them came with Mica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 7, paragraph 28. On the fourth day of your detention, were three other men brought in from Bijeljina whom you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us names and, so far as relevant, occupation of those men?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smajic Ejub, who was a butcher. Ferid Zecevic. He had a coffee shop, a restaurant. And Zlatan was a jeweller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what, if anything, Ferid Zecevic had done with his money, he being the restaurateur, before being brought to the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the Bajram holiday, Arkan went to him and took money so that nobody could touch him. So Arkan went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, when these three men were brought to the SUP building, how were they treated?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked anything, they just beat you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these three men were beaten as were you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and these three others thereafter taken to the Batkovic detention camp which is near Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see this on page 29, immediately to the north of Bijeljina in square E2 on the right-hand side. Was that camp -- or did that camp consist of two hangars and two tents?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it fenced with wire some two metres high with barbed wire on top and with two guard towers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly how many people were detained there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 2.000, perhaps more. About 2.000 anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ethnic composition of those detained?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of these detained? Were they Serbs? Were they Muslims? Were they Croats?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly they were Muslims, but there were some Croats too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any elderly people there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And any women?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was one woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the age of the youngest children there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were very small children, young children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the ICRC, the International Committee of the Red Cross, visit the camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did visit, but the older children and the smaller children, there were ten special purpose soldiers, and they would hide the children so -- when the Red Cross came to register.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of the children released after the Red Cross visit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The children were not released, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as these detainees were concerned, were they civilians, or combatants, or mostly civilians or mostly combatants, or what?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were just two combatants who had been captured, and they were called the Green Berets. All the others were civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which local towns and villages did the detainees mostly come?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brcko, Zvornik, Vlasenica, Bijeljina, Brezovo Polje, Koraj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any other towns from which they came, any larger towns?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, of course. If other places come back to you, please tell us. The guards at the camp, where did they mostly come from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning when I had just been arrested, there was a warrant officer from Novi Sad. I don't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of his deputy at all and where he came from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the deputy was Veljo. What -- he was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first arrived at the camp, did you see what happened to Ferid Zecevic and Ejub Smajic? Paragraph 33.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was beating and beating, and Ferid just couldn't take it, and he succumbed the first night to the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did the beating?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it was Veljo who did the beating, with a mask, with a sock over his head. And Gligor, Zoran. There was a major of some kind there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Veljo, do you know his last name?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember it now but I do know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this one of the guards who did the beating?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljo, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljo was the deputy, the deputy of this warrant officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you put his name in your statement? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, or maybe I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I mention to the witness the name Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the name that you connect with Veljo or Veljko?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what he called -- they called him, but I don't know the surname exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there another man involved in these beatings in some way who went by the nickname of Piklic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Piklic was a Muslim, and he broke my ribs and my spine and everything else. One hundred and twenty kilos, he was, and he stood on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Piklic was his nickname. Do you know what his real name was?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what everyone called him, Piklic. I did know his name, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Explain, please, how this man, a Muslim, came to be beating you in the way that you've described.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not one, two of them, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the other Muslim who was beating you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spajzer. I think his name was Dzemal Zahirovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain how these two Muslims were beating you and injuring you in the way that you've described.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why they did. Perhaps to gave their own heads. And they couldn't care less for other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained how one of the two men attacked succumbed pretty quickly. What happened to the other one? Did he die as well?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on the third day Zlatan, the jeweller, he also succumbed. He couldn't take it any more. So myself and Smajic were left. The two of us were left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were still being beaten by, amongst others, these two Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided with any food in the camp? If so, describe it.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were given food, but I couldn't eat it because they would beat you up first and then give you the food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you obliged to do any work, labour?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time, but not afterwards. I was -- I seemed to be a speciality for being beaten up, as if I was to blame for the war and so that people could see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the two men you've described as dying the only ones who to your knowledge died or did others die? If so, how many?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the number might have been up to 100 people certainly. They succumbed, older ones, others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the problems with food, were conditions very hot?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was very hot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of the combination of factors, beating, lack of food, and heat, were you from time to time actually taken as dead while you were still alive?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They took me out four times because they thought I was dead, but I seem to have lived on. I would move a leg or an arm and they would take me back again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of Mauzer's men visit the camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were different soldiers. As soon as they came, they would look for us special ones, and there were ten of us, and beat us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we come to the special ten of you to whom I'll turn, when Mauzer's men visited the camp, did they do anything else in relation to the property of any other detainees?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would take us to a place to hide us and take money and gold from people who had it on them. Well, they didn't have anything to take from me, because even my T-shirt was torn. So all this beating was on my bare body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The group of ten special men, did that include initially Ferid Zecevic and Ejub Smajic who died from beatings?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was always a group of ten people. And if one person would succumb to the beatings, then they would make up the number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any of the ones who made up in this way the group of ten specials? Give us some other names.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rebic Cedo from Brcko, Tufekcic Andrija from Brcko, Mustafic Saban. That was a young person of 16. Kuralic Mirsad. Mostacevic Nedim. Alihodzic Fadil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The ten of you -- or the changing group of the ten of you, were you given special treatment? If so, what?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the hangar was actually for everyone, but the rest of the people making up the 2.000, nobody dared contact -- make any contact with us. And if somebody did have any contacts with us, then he would be transferred to our group and beaten, so that the people didn't want to risk talking to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how regularly were the group of ten beaten; every day or more than once a day, or what?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Breakfast, lunch, dinner, when we lined up, and midnight, after 12.00. And they would beat us unconscious then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you lose weight in the course of this treatment, and if so, how much so that you're -- how much did you lose and how much did you ultimately weigh?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I weighed 109 or 110 kilos before, and during the time I was there, when I was in Batkovici for the first time, I went down to 59 kilos, which, for a large man like myself, is a lot of weight loss. I was just skin and bone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've said a little about the Red Cross visits. Tell us again, what happened to this group of ten specials when the ICRC came?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know -- well, as soon as they hear that the Red Cross is coming, they take us away from the hangar some 500 kilometres [as interpreted] away, where the livestock was kept, and that's where they hid us. Cardak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there one other particular event, or two other particular events that occurred? First of all, was there something about standing on a chair involving a noose that you can tell us about?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very difficult. When the Red Cross came, they hung me. They tried everything else, and then that's what they tried ultimately too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they hung you, are you describing a hanging by a noose and by your neck, and was it with an intention to kill you or simply to restrain you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To torment me. They tried everything. They beat me, and then they tried that too to see what that would look like, what effect that would have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there sexual activity that was forced on you? If so, in a sentence, tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's shame on them to force a man to sleep with a man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that done once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it done in the hangar or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Cardak, when we were hidden away, when the Red Cross would used to arrive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so who was looking at this, just the guards and the other members of the ten or who else?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards there. The guards were the ones who worked there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Around September 1992, did you move or were you moved from this camp to the camp at Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think it's necessary to produce a separate exhibit. The Chamber can see it on page 28 of the atlas, pretty well in the middle of the page, in block C2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went, did you go with other members of the special group of ten?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same group, ten of us. Us ten of us went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On arrival were you examined?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the garrison in Doboj, that's where. But we were living corpses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the doctors who examined you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did a good job. I was covered in wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed had some --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With maggots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With maggots. Thank you. And how did they treat you, the doctors?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fairly well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity of looking at yourself in a mirror?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I got a fright when I saw myself. I didn't look like a human being at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following medical examination, were you taken to a camp in some army warehouses?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Usora camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the name of the camp may be different from that which is used in the indictment, and for that reason I'll ask the next question, but the Chamber will see the river Usora running out of Doboj south and west of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Usora camp as you describe it, was it close to a particular factory?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a fruit factory, Bosanka, and we went to work there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it similar in composition as to hangars and so on to the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Similar. Well, the hangars were the same, but there were less people there. And they even kept Serbs there, the Serbs who didn't want to go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Muslims were there there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the ten of us and perhaps a hundred people. Not more than that ever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Croat detainees?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andrija was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's one Croat, is it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were kept at this camp for about how long?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eleven and a half months, I think it was. Eleven, eleven and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that period of detention typical for other detainees as well?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In the course of your time at this camp, were there several commanders?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming from what force?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was one of them by name Ziko Novic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the guards, did they also come from the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that one of them was a Montenegrin, but I can't remember his name just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the others?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly Serbian from the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were conditions in this camp better, worse, or about the same as in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were better. They were better for me. Better because I was beaten less there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you still beaten?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they beat us with police batons, and that was just like a game, like a toy compared to the rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever hit you on your faces?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, not that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any prisoners dying at this camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but there were wounded people, injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name any of the guards who did mistreat detainees?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Dzuro Martic. He was commander of the military police. He would come by frequently. And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any Serb prisoner, those who were being detained because they were unwilling to fight, was any Serb prisoner involved in beating other detainees?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were in the first hangar, and the Muslims and Croats in the second and third.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us the name of any such prisoner -- name or nickname of any such Serb prisoner who beat other detainees?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was someone we called Tropek, with three fingers. Two cut off and three remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would come in often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I turn to paragraph 47, forced labour. Were you, during your period at this camp, taken to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this forced or voluntary work?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it was forced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any prisoners die while digging trenches close to the frontline?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you to think again. Can you remember any incidents at the frontline, when trench digging was going on, of prisoners being wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many prisoners were wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that had happened, were they replaced and did the work continue or was work suspended?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Work was continued, and they were taken away to be -- for their wounds to be dressed and later on back to the hangars probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On one occasion when digging trenches, were you taken to a village called Smajne Vode?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It does not show up on the map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can't find this -- at least, I can't find this on the map that we have. Can you help us at all with how near to or far from Doboj this village was?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's right next to Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were preparing digging trenches. This was a village that had signed its loyalty that it wouldn't go to war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find in the village by way of bodies of people?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, they attacked the village, and in one house after that attack, there were up to 40 civilians, some killed, some slaughtered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who attacked the village? Who attacked the village? I didn't catch your answer, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chetniks, the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say they were slaughtered, did you see how they'd been slaughtered? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I loaded them onto a truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how had they been killed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them had their throats slit, and there were others who had been killed with shots from firearms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your working party had to deal with them by loading them onto a truck and taking them where? Or don't you know where they went?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We loaded them onto the trucks, and they drove them off, I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also from time to time obliged to cut wood for those who were fighting?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross visit the camp? If so, roughly how many months into your detention?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think after five or six months, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did conditions change after the Red Cross visit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, we were given clothing and it was better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your wife allowed to visit you in due course?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she would come to visit me with our son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did she visit you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Two or three times. But after that, we would again be beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of - paragraph 52 - of other prisoners being kept in the police station in the centre of Doboj town?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a man called Jelisic, Goran Jelisic, from before the war, a man coming from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of detention, were you spoken to by other detainees, one named Djelo Kamberi and another named Andrija Tufekcic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were elite specials, and we were in that group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you what Jelisic had done in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had spent some time in Brcko, and they knew Jelisic well in those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you of Jelisic's doings in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there was a manhole where he killed people. And even Andrija's turn had come, but somehow he managed to escape. He had the good luck not to be killed by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anything said about the numbers of people that Jelisic had killed in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figures were high. They also mentioned someone called Monika.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it said Monika had done?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That she too had done the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said the figures are high, are we dealing in fives, tens, twenties, or more?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the figures were over a hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you taken from Doboj after your eleven and a half months back to Batkovic with four other of the special group of ten?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had the other five already been exchanged at or during their time in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you kept at Batkovic for another three months?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was supposed to be exchanged, but -- the exchange was all for all, but they left me behind and the others left. And so I stayed there for another three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this occasion, roughly how many Muslim men were there there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. On this occasion, your second detention in Batkovic, roughly how many Muslim detainees were there there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number was between 800 and 900, but the following few days, about 600 or 700 had been exchanged, and I was supposed to go with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this occasion, were there any beatings or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, no one beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge and on information, were there included in the detainees people from the Manjaca camp and from the Rogatica camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was the only one from the Tuzla region, and there were some from Manjaca, about a hundred to 150 men. And from Rogatica also there were some.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interrogated from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't beat me, but they mistreated me psychologically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness now see on the computer Exhibit 414, tab 3, which is a list of prisoners of war of Muslim ethnicity exchanged on a date in October 1993, the document coming from a report on the commission of exchange of prisoners of war and the report suggesting that the names are the names of detainees from the Batkovic camp. If we can make sure I have the same screen that the witness has.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the witness to read out the limited number of names he recognises - they have already been highlighted - in order that the names can be on the searchable computer LiveNote record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at this list of names, Mr. Gusalic, did you recognise number 6, Anto Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go down to number 10, and would you read out the name if it's a name you recognise.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okanovic, Ilijaz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eleven?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's me, Alija Gusalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Forty-four?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Omerovic Beniz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 56. If you can find that.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Lovric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are all names that you recognise as having been in the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your second detention there, of course.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple of other tiny points or small points. At your first detention in Batkovic, were you interviewed on television or for television --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- by a member of the Serb Radical Party called Pusula, together with some foreign journalists including one apparently from Russia?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the village of Trnova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That I think one can see on the map. I found it before. I hadn't marked it. Yes, it's just south and west of Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just south and west of Bijeljina. During your second detention -- I beg your pardon. Go back. In this interview, were you invited to say things that were true or invited to say things that were false?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were false, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you forced to say things that were false or did you decline to cooperate?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was promised if I said that the Muslims had started the war, that they would take me to see my wife and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in fact say things that were false or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I say something that wasn't true?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, at paragraph 59 of the summary, the spelling of "Trnava" is wrong. It should be T-R-N-O-V-A, not A-V-A, if the map is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your second period of detention in Batkovic, were you interviewed on several occasions by civilians, and did these civilians include television crews from the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say things that were false or did you decline to do so?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always spoke the truth, and perhaps that is why I suffered so much. The truth must win.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as property is concerned, your town of Bijeljina, how many mosques had there been there before the war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five, and the sixth one was under construction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they damaged at all in the course of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were destroyed totally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Janja a village in the municipality of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see it immediately south and just before you reach the river and the border. Were there two mosques there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to them in the war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were also destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your present condition is that you still suffer from pain in your chest, arms, and back; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You suffer diabetes, apparently connected to the events that you've described and the suffering that you underwent?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I developed diabetes in 1997.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the date of your exchange?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 8th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you wait there, you will be asked some further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gusalic, you lived in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as I can see from your statement, you don't dare return to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I return to Bijeljina when I lost my health, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But tell me, I assume you would feel better in your own town. Are you afraid of something? Are you afraid of returning to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you afraid of?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid of those men who inflicted what they did to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're afraid of men who are today living in Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is why you don't dare return there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is perhaps the reason for your fear that a large number of people say about you that you were the man who started the war in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I started the war, Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm asking you whether that is true.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can that be true?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because there are certain facts confirming this. For example, before I move any further, the other day I received from the side opposite - this is not my document - a statement of Esad Brkic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, this was disclosed to me under Rule 68, Esad Brkic's statement, and the first page is 00212764, and I will quote from page 11 of this statement which is marked, of the opposing side, 00212774. So it is a statement by a Muslim, which is quite a lengthy statement. "Gusalic, the day prior to the beginning of the war in Bijeljina, in a tipsy condition, got on a horse and with a flag of the SDA - that is the Party of Democratic Action, this nationalist Muslim extremist party - the Party of Democratic Action, holding that flag in one hand and a grenade in the other, entered a coffee shop in Bijeljina, threw the grenade, which didn't go off. The Serb owner of the restaurant opened fire, shot him, and wounded him."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what is being claimed not by Serbs, though they say the same, but here you have this statement by a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. Yes, Mr. Gusalic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, that's a lie regarding the flag. I didn't have a flag, Mr. Milosevic, but I did have a grenade. And I am sorry now that I didn't throw the grenade into that coffee shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you throw it in or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that unfortunately I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, where was that bomb?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in my hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far were you from that coffee shop with that bomb?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 to 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And your intention was to throw the bomb?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because Arkan's, Seselj's, and Mirko's men were in that cafe. There were no civilians there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. Who was in the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally know who was in there, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were a few metres away from the coffee shop with this bomb in your hand, and everyone can see you carrying this bomb and that you intended to throw it in there; is that right? So it was quite clear to everyone in that cafe that you intended to throw the bomb at them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two guards in front, armed guards in front of that cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, whether they were guards or not, it's rather unbelievable, but it was quite clear that you were carrying this hand grenade and intended to throw it at the Srbija coffee bar. You were wounded there. Where were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your leg. And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the hospital, and I escaped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who took you to hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. I won't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't those same men who had wounded you and who had prevented you from throwing the grenade take you to hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They continued shooting, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They continued shooting at you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were shooting towards the Istanbul coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. We'll come to that later. Now, tell me, please, is it true that you went to the Radojka Lakic elementary school?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is totally irrelevant. That's a most improper question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No, it is not a proper question, and the witness will not have to answer it. Now, kindly confine yourself to what is relevant and proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May that passage be redacted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, go on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shame on you, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, I can understand that you'll be annoyed, but try not to be. You will be protected from questions of that sort. You're not here to harry the witnesses or bully them, Mr. Milosevic. Now you'll confine yourself to proper questions. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I think that this is proof that Mr. Nice is abusing this witness. He is obtaining statements from him which are not truthful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can ask the witness proper questions. Now, get -- move on to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For instance, Mr. May, a moment ago we heard Mr. Nice's questions having to do with certain men found with their throats slit which they carried, buried, and so on, and I noted this down. This was some 15 or 20 minutes ago, in front of all of us; that they found them, that they were civilians, some had been shot, some had their throat slit. And I was surprised, because I didn't pay attention to that when I read the statement of the witness. I reread it quickly. There's not a word about it. Where did this come from now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Of course you can put the statement to the witness. That's a perfectly proper form of cross-examination. What isn't is to abuse them. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, if what you just said is true, how come that you didn't consider it important to tell the investigators when you were making your statement? How come you forgot such a "minute" matter regarding some 40 people killed and slaughtered and now you suddenly remembered such an event? How is that possible? Could you explain that for me?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my life I never lied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is clear. But how come you didn't say that in your statement? Why is that not in your statement and you suddenly remembered finding these people?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That should be in the statement. I think it should be in the statement. Read that statement more carefully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if it is in the statement, I'll withdraw this question. There's no problems whatsoever. We can move on now. You say that you're not a member of any political party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to my information, you are a member of the Party of Democratic Action from its very foundation. So you're not.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're making me laugh. I have a mixed marriage. My first marriage and my second marriage was a mixed marriage. I was not interested in the war, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but are you living in that mixed marriage with your wife?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you get on well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have two wives, and both are Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you have two wives?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they are both Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, maybe the information I have is incorrect, because I don't know anyone in Bijeljina so I can only talk about what I heard from others. Is it true that you were convicted several times before the war because of various incidents, fights, provoking squabbles on an ethnic basis? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were never convicted?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a convenient time. We will adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, a moment ago, you told me about some bodies and people whose throats had been slit, and you said that it must have been in the statement. I have taken a look at your statement during the break, and this is what it says in your statement. It's on page 9 of your statement, and you say: "In the camp in Doboj, I stayed for eleven and a half months. We had to dig trenches up at the front but not during the shooting." That's what it says in your statement. Then you go on to say: "During the fighting, we would have to take out the bodies of the killed Serb soldiers from the front." That's what you also state.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, read it once again. It must be there somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, read the statement with greater care. It must be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you find what you claim you say in your statement, please.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I have only completed eight years of schooling, and I can't read. I don't know how to read.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can't read through it. Perhaps the opposite side can help me and find what you claim you say in your statement about those slaughtered persons.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about 40 of them. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, help us with this. Mr. Nice, do you want to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was going to respond to the accused's invitation by saying this is a matter that, as I understood it, emerged first in proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Well, at least we've cleared that point up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Mirko Blagojevic, and you said that people gathered there, Chetniks with beards, as you say, and so on. So what colour was Mirko Blagojevic's beard? Was it black or was it grey, white?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Blagojevic didn't have any colour. He didn't have a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean so others had a beard?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the co-owner of the house in which the Srbija coffee bar was located, the co-owner, and actually the entrance is the same, just half a metre one from another, the co-owner's name is Demir Dizdarevic, and he's a Muslim. Do you know of him? Have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know that in the coffee bar itself, when you wanted to throw your hand grenade inside, that there were Serbs and Muslims inside?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in the coffee bar, and I saw who was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you claim that it wasn't Serbs and Croats who were inside?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean, that there were or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there were only Serbs inside; Arkan's men, Seselj's men, and Mirko's men, armed to the teeth. Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my information tells me that nobody was armed. There was just one pistol that somebody had borrowed, of the 7.65 millimetre calibre type, and that they shot at you from that pistol when you started throwing the bomb.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a lie, sir. You haven't been informed correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there are other people who were there, so we'll be able to clear that up. But let's move on for now. You say that the soldiers who entered the coffee bar called Srbija, and you say that in your statement on page 2, paragraph 6, that they were wearing camouflage uniforms, that they did not have any special caps. How can an ordinary army have any special caps, and what kind of caps did they wear at all? Tell me that.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were soldiers, different types of soldiers there. The radicals, they had the cockade type of caps. The others had the panthers or, rather, the tiger insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the basis of what do you draw your conclusion that they were Arkan's and Seselj's men, as you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had a different accent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we talk differently from the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you made your observations and conclusions on the basis of accent whether somebody was from Serbia and from Bijeljina and so on?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if they say that they were people from Bijeljina there, would that be a lie? Would that not be the truth?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could it be the truth?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me this: As you said that Mirko Blagojevic was a functionary of the Serbian Radical Party, and you say there were no Muslims and so on and so forth, do you know or have you heard about a man whose name was Izet Selihbegovic, nicknamed Izo Beg? Have you ever heard of him? You're from Bijeljina yourself.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know that this Muslim, Izo Beg, is the secretary of the Serbian Radical Party? Is that true? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it's correct and true but I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard about it. Right. Now, how then do you explain that a party of any kind, as you say, is persecuting the Muslims whereas the secretary of the party itself is a Muslim himself?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe he changed his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say? Changed what?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Izo Beg hasn't changed his name.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that even before the war he was a deputy of the Serbian Radical Party in the Bijeljina municipality, for example?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't delve in politics much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that at the last parliamentary elections he was a candidate put forward by the Serbian Radical Party for the parliament of Republika Srpska? He was on their ticket of the Serbian Radical Party. But anyway, yesterday in the examination-in-chief, you started off by making an observation, and that was that your brothers were in the army of Republika Srpska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how then do you explain -- and your brothers are of course Muslims like yourself.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain, then, that they were in the army of Republika Srpska if that army of Republika Srpska, as you say, persecuted Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they went up to the frontline. They pushed the Muslims to the frontline so that Muslims could kill Muslims. So they were forced to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you wish to say that they were forced?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes of course. They wouldn't go as volunteers, would they?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So they weren't in the army of Republika Srpska voluntarily, of their own free will. They didn't bear arms of their own free will and fight voluntarily in those ranks?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how would they be volunteers to shoot at their own people, to shoot at me as their brother? There's no logic there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this was a confrontation and conflict with Muslim extremists and not a conflict with the Muslims as such. Is that so or not, Mr. Gusalic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and after a year in Republika Srpska and the Serbian army, they had to flee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you yourself are from Bijeljina, and as you say that the Muslims were allegedly there by force, that they were forced to be there, do you know that the 3rd Semberija Brigade which was deployed in Bijeljina and in the environs in Bijeljina, further afield, numbered several thousand fighters, 95 per cent of those were Muslims? Are you aware of that? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard about Major Pasaga Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't, and I'm not interested either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Pasaga Halilovic --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that. I'm not going to answer those questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're duty-bound to answer. You can say you don't know, but you can't say that you refuse to answer questions.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know and I'm not going to answer that. I don't know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you believe that there is a man in Bijeljina -- that there can be a man in Bijeljina, a single person who hasn't heard of Major Pasaga Halilovic? Do you know that he was the director of the Duvan factory?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If you haven't heard of Pasaga Halilovic, who was the commander of the brigade which was composed of Muslims and was within the composition of the army of Republika Srpska, have you heard of Major Sejfudin Guri, for example, who was the Chief of Staff of that particular unit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you haven't heard of Sejfudin Guri either. And he was also a professor teaching protection and self-defence at the agricultural school before the war. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of Captain Sead Tikvec then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of Captain Hajrudin Hajro, who was commander of the artillery in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in the VRS, the army of Republika Srpska, the 3rd Semberija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't heard of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was almost 100 per cent Muslim.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would appear, sir, that the Serbs didn't go into battle at all, that it was just the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that many Muslims from Bijeljina resisted the attacks and stood up to the attacks launched by extremists who had blocked Bijeljina and who were engaged in attacking the region. These are people who still live in Bijeljina today and who without a doubt are Muslims themselves. Sir, have you heard of Dr. Nedzad Havic, for example, who was head of the medical corps in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't heard about him either?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what about Joldic Jusuf? Does the name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Samir Joldic? Do you know him? They're all people from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know them. If they were there in Bijeljina, well, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Alija Omerovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Salcin Mehic or Alija Durakovic? Do you know them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They're all from Bijeljina. How about Ramo Durakovic and Sead Becirovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're quoting names, the whole of Bijeljina, but I don't know any of them who were in the Republika Srpska.
