utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Alija Berberovic, or Emil Vilic? Do you know them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or Ferid Teric?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, all right. I'm not going to read out any more names. The list is a long one. They're all the names of Muslims who were in the units of the army of Republika Srpska, precisely from your town, Bijeljina, and you're testifying about that. And do you know that that particular brigade held a whole section of the front which ran for dozens of kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And are you saying they all went on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if they didn't want to go to the front, they could have turned round and gone back. It was a whole brigade. There couldn't have been anybody behind them.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but where were their families? They left their families behind. You leave your family and they send you to the front. You escape to the other side and they kill your wife and children, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the whole brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the whole brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then that's a very good explanation that you've just given. My information tells me that the unit held positions from Orasje to Brcko.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And where were their families? An example: My brothers. They went to the front line, and their families remained in Bijeljina. Had they tried to escape, their families would have been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that apart from Bijeljina another well-known Muslim unit within the composition of the army of Republika Srpska was the Mesa Selimovic detachment from Derventa. Have you heard of them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several thousand Muslims in that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you're saying you know nothing about all that, and you consider that the facts I have just quoted are not correct and true. All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They can't be correct and true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Very well. Now, tell me this: As you claim that in the village of Amajlije --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- members of some Serb formations were put up, accommodated.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I wrote -- made a note of this yesterday, of what you said. You said that whoever comes to Amajlije was either slaughtered or tortured because it was a kind of camp.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there was no camp at all in Amajlije, or any formations or units.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I claim on the basis of my information.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that's not right, sir. There was one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a centre in the village of Popovi which is quite opposite to Amajlije.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the village of Amajlije, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. As you say so. We'll be able to establish the truth very easily on that point. Now, tell me this, please, since you didn't know about Izo Beg, you hadn't heard of him who was the secretary of the Serbian Radical Party, do you happen to know Albin Arifovic, the son of the president of the municipality of Bijeljina, Saki Arifovic, the mayor of the municipality, and this Albin Arifovic was a man who worked in the coffee bar named Srbija, Srbija.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was a Muslim. He was an employee there.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Professor Rasim Jusupovic? Have you heard of him? Have you heard of Professor Rasim Jusupovic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He gave an interview for the Muslim media in the year 2000 in which he said that the Muslims had a great deal of protection from this man Mirko Blagojevic whom you blame and hold responsible of the leader of the Serbian Radical Party in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he -- people want to go back and they have nowhere to go back to, sir. I'm not interested in Bijeljina, sir. I've lost my health, and I have no intention of going back there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of an open letter written by Mirko Blagojevic and dated 1992, sent to all the authorities, telling them that the Serbian authorities from Bijeljina will not allow any hair of the Muslims' head to be harmed or allow any Muslim, not a single Muslim, to be expelled from Bijeljina? Do you know about that letter?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That nothing would happen.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing will happen but they will be slaughtered, their throats will be slit. What did he do with Redzep and Cosa?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to Cosa in due course.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you've just asked me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you that. You're speaking untruths when you say that Cosa's sister told you that Cosa had been killed.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when she came to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This sister of Cosa's gave an interview to the Sarajevo paper Oslobodjenje and said that he died at home. So in her interview that's what she says.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say, died?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer the question. It's been put that this man died at home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He died voluntarily, did he? Of his own free will?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that anybody dies of their own free will, voluntarily, but between being killed and dying in your own home, there's a big difference.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was completely deformed. There are witnesses, sir, who saw him personally and would be able to testify. He didn't have a human face any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what his sister said for the Sarajevo Oslobodjenje is probably a lie, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. That's a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Jasmin Sabic, nicknamed Jasko, who used to work in the sugar factory and moved to Switzerland and who is still a sympathiser of the Serbian Radical Party to this day and one of their sponsors? Do you know of him? And he lives in Switzerland, so nobody can persecute him there, can they?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he sent money for the army of Republika Srpska, did he? What did you say? That he sent money?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't say that he sent money for the army of Republika Srpska. What I said was that he was a sympathiser of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We are not being helped by this particularly about events at the moment. So let's move on to something else rather than reading out a series of names about which the witness knows nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, on page 3, paragraph 1, you speak about an incident that took place when a bomb, a grenade was thrown at the Cafe Istanbul; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the bomb was thrown by a man called Goran.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; Goran or Zoran, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you happen to know, because there are documents to evidence this, first that the incident took place some ten days prior to the outbreak of the war, not one day before the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten days you say? What did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ten days before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am satisfied with any of your answers, whether you say yes or no, because we'll be able to establish the truth. Now, do you know that the man who threw the bomb was not called Goran?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was either Goran or Zoran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your statement you say that this was not established, and my information tells me that the man's name was Aleksandar Zekic, that he was from Dvorovi near Bijeljina, and that he was arrested straight away and taken off to the prison in Tuzla on order from the head of the Secretariat for Internal Affairs in Bijeljina, and his name was Jesuric Predrag, the man who issued the orders. But this Aleksandar Zekovic was nicknamed Andalaga, and he threw the bomb, he was arrested and taken off to the prison in Tuzla. And all this took place about ten days before the war broke out. So the police intervened and arrested the man.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I've stopped your microphone because you're going on much too long. There are a series of questions there. We'll go through them one by one. What is suggested by the accused, and you can help us or not, Mr. Gusalic, is that the man who threw the bomb was called Aleksandar Zekic. That's what he suggests. Can you help us as to whether that is or may be the case or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know his name for sure, but I know he's from Dvorovi. I thought his name was Zoran.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next point is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is true that he was taken to the prison in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So have we cleared that up? Have we also cleared up the fact that this was about ten days before the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how many days prior to the beginning of the war was this incident in which this man threw the grenade and was arrested and taken to prison by order of the chief of the SUP, a Serb, Jesuric Predrag?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all Serbs, or most of them were Serbs in the SUP in the larger towns, mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is normal in Bijeljina that most of them should be Serbs, because Bijeljina was mostly inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Bijeljina as such was a Muslim majority. The town had a majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it doesn't matter. That's easy to establish. We have a population census, and it's easy to know. There is no point in us bothering over that. Do you know that this guy, this man who threw the grenade, was arrested, taken to Tuzla, that he was a mental patient and an alcoholic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that. Apparently when you're talking, everyone was a mental patient that graduated from special schools.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Quite the opposite. Only the individuals, specific individuals that I mentioned. They are data that I have. So regardless of the fact that he was a mental patient and an alcoholic, he was arrested and taken to the prison in Tuzla because he did what he did. He was arrested by Serbs and taken to the prison by Serbs. But very well. In your statement you said that in those days in the Istanbul coffee bar, seven Muslims were wounded; five men and two women. This is stated in your statement. Is this what you said?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some wounded Serb as well, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to ask you about, Mr. Gusalic. Do you know the name of Goran Vasalic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. You know him. He is the man known as Goran Kriska, a well-known basketball player from Bijeljina. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he's the Vasilic man. Do you know that he's a Serb and that he lives in the area called Kriska?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that this Goran was wounded in that very Istanbul coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in hospital with you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that a young woman called Sofija, also a Serb woman, was wounded at that same attack?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that, Mr. Milosevic, yes. I do know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you think that this attack can be described as an attack by a Serb nationalist against Muslims or was it an attack by an alcoholic who couldn't account for his actions and who committed a crime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't bother to answer that. Characterisation of the attack is not for the witness. He can mainly give evidence purely about what happened. It's not for him to describe it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Since I have information here that there was a spirit of tolerance between Serbs and Muslims in Bijeljina, that they lived in harmony right up until that day when the Green Berets and the so-called League blocked Bijeljina and set up barricades and captured, took control of Bijeljina. Do you know that, for instance, in the Srbija coffee bar, owned by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've put things -- you can't simply put things and just pass by. The first question -- two questions in what's been put, Mr. Gusalic. The first question: Was there a spirit of tolerance between the Serbs and Muslims in Bijeljina before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The next question: And that was broken up, if you will, when the Green Berets set up barricades and captured, it's said, and took control of Bijeljina. Did the Green Berets take control of Bijeljina, first of all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what Mr. Milosevic implies under the Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Don't worry about that for the moment, what he means by the Green Berets. Let's look at it another way. Was it a Muslim force of some sort who broke up the previous spirit of tolerance and harmony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what to say. There was tension.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just tell us how it happened. Just explain to us how it all started, if you will.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was tension because people were coming from Serbia to this village of Amajlije that Mr. Milosevic says I'm lying about, and this was common knowledge, that attack was being prepared on Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Are you denying that apart from the incidents we described, there was nothing until the Green Berets and members of the Patriotic League of People, Muslim formations, took over control of Bijeljina, erected barricades, and blocked the whole city? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everyone has to defend himself when he sees that somebody wants to kill him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they defending themselves against when nothing had happened before that? Why did they block the town, erect barricades and distribute weapons? Why? Had anyone attacked them before that? Or were they expecting to be attacked and that's why they did that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know all the places that were blocked and where the roadblocks were set up?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the Muslims. So you don't know about that? No?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's fine. We have some other witnesses here and we'll be able to clear that up with them. Now, tell me, please, what was Izet Gogic doing, known as Goga the Gypsy?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was he called?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Goga the Gypsy. That's what it says in my notes here.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, he's not a Gypsy, he's a Muslim. And he worked privately. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is what he did.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked as a mason, as a private builder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you meet?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had known each other for some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that just before the war he was a horse carriage driver?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was given money by your party, the SDA, to open a coffee bar? That is he was given this money by Ferid Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Mirko Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. I'm talking about Izet Gogic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you think Mirko gave him money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm saying that he got money from the SDA. Not from SRS but from the SDA, from Ferid Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. That's something you didn't note down well in your record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Izet Gogic and Cosa the Boxer, is that right, they spoke to you before you started off to throw the grenade. Did they persuade you to do that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody persuaded me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave you the bomb?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goga gave it to me because I didn't have the money to buy one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Goga gave you the bomb. Was Cosa there too?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were there together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they told you to go and throw the bomb into the Cafe Srbija?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one told me, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they gave you a bomb to play with?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They gave me the bomb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how much time Cosa the Boxer had spent in prison?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that he was convicted to prison sentences for several years on several occasions for various criminal offences? You know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's fine. And you are claiming that he was killed rather than dying at home.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he was killed. He was massacred. He was mutilated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Cosa's sister is married to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where she lives now?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what are we going on about here? You're wasting a great deal of time, it seems to be, quite unnecessarily with these side issues. Remember, your time is limited. This witness has given very serious evidence about what happened him to in the camps. If you challenge that, if you suggest it's not true, then you should do so while he's here giving evidence instead of wasting time in this way with side issues. If you don't challenge it, of course we accept the evidence, but if you do challenge it, you should cross-examine him about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Surely it is clear, Mr. May, that I am denying all his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it -- do you know that this same Cosa brought men from Sandzak --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Never mind the statements. You should move on to the camps. Your time is limited. If you're suggesting that what he said about what happened in the camps isn't true in some way, then you should put that part of the case to him instead of these side issues. Now, move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, do you consider it to be a side issue as to how the war in Bijeljina started, how the Green Berets blocked Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have spent the best part of 40 minutes on this. Your time is limited. You have had probably more than half of it. You should move on to something else. The witness says he can't help any more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move on to something else to meet your request, Mr. May, since you're talking about camps. I have here two documents which I also received from the side opposite under Rule 68 disclosure. For one, I don't know what it is at all because I was only given two pages, pages four and five of it. They probably felt that they didn't need to give me the whole document. It is marked 00290957, and it's a report which speaks about -- what was its name? Batkovic. Batkovic. And it says: [In English] "Approximately 1.000 Muslim prisoners was visited in Batkovic in north-eastern Bosnia. The prisoners did not complain of ill-treatment, and in general, appeared to be in good health. However, they sleep on straw bedding on the floor of a cavernous unheated stable where living conditions will become intolerable as the cold weather arrives." [Interpretation] I'm reading with interruptions because I'm listening to the interpreters, and I would like it to be correctly interpreted to the witness, as it has been done indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Mr. Gusalic, can you comment on this? As far as I'm able to tell, this is a report of the International Red Cross that visited Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, they're saying here that the prisoners are not complaining of ill-treatment and that, generally speaking, they appear to be in good health. That is what is stated in the report. I gave the page that I was given from the party opposite. It is no report of mine. So is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not true. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think the report is not Red Cross but Special Rapporteur of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have we got the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have the same extract that's been served on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We may have an extract.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, because we haven't served the entire report. I can dig it out and see how much it amounts to in full but I think it's UN Special Rapporteur not Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The sensible thing, I think, would be to mark it for identification for the moment and for you to produce, if you would, the relevant parts of the original so that we can have it in front us, including a date of the inspection. We'll mark it for identification and we'll get the original out of the Prosecution and we will exhibit it. Perhaps we'll have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Defence Exhibit 114, Your Honours, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. If you'd like to hand in those two pages so that a copy can be made.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you can take them. And I have highlighted the part that I have quoted. I was only given those two pages in this connection. And now I have another report which was also served on me under Rule 68 disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm sorry. Move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this, as far as I am able to gather, is a report by Reuters dated 1993. Actually, the copyright is 1993, the 26th of February, but it doesn't say which year, and I'll only quote a couple of paragraphs from it: "Bosnian Serbs set up Batkovic [in English] farm which functions normally on the flat lands around soon after the start of the war last April, described as a collection centre for Muslims and Croats who in any way participated in combat activities or collecting weapons and ammunition. There is no obvious rancor between prisoners and Serbs, and the International Red Cross visits every week." [Interpretation] This was given to me in its entirety, and at the end, since they're interviewing this Savic who, as I am able to gather, was some sort of an official over there, and it says: [In English] "Returning Serbs were in worse physical condition than Muslims and Croats from Batkovic, that there is no evidence of violence or malnutrition."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is what I have quoted from the document and contained in the document correct or not, Mr. Gusalic? You can say yes or no, whichever you like, and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like to tender this as well. Could you please include this document, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Milosevic, that is a pure lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It says two things. First of all, it was merely a collection centre for Muslims and Croats who had participated in combat activities. Is there any truth in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No truth whatsoever. They were all civilians. Just two young guys were captured who were up at the frontline. They were otherwise all women, children, and elderly persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the International Red Cross every week paid a visit, as it says in this statement? This is not a Serbian statement or report.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was every week, but, yes, it did come by often, and they did not register the ten of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not the ten of you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The ten of us who were beaten, the specials. The elderly persons were not recorded either, nor were the children. The Yugoslav army, the Muslims who were released, dismissed, they too were not registered. They were hidden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who then was registered? All right. Well, we'll be able to establish that. I just wish to ascertain one point. You yourself were not registered. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you read your name from the list a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was registered in Doboj, in Doboj camp, not in Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you read out, is that from the Doboj camp, the list you read out from? Was the list from the Doboj camp?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the young guys who were in Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you're on that same list, aren't you? So how do you say that you weren't registered if you can read your name from the list?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You and I speak the same language, and I said that we were registered in Doboj. In the first two and a half or three months, I was beaten and hidden away and then transported to Doboj where the Red Cross found me later. Somebody told them. And the ten of us were registered then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I cannot accept that explanation of yours.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't have to accept anything, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to those events when the war broke out in Bijeljina, how many people from Sandzak did you see and how many Albanians from Kosovo did you see? How many of one and how many of the other? You can give me separate figures.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Roughly. A rough estimate. I don't -- I'm not asking for an exact figure.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see a single one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see a single one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see a single one. And do you know that it was precisely this man Cosa who you say was a friend of yours who brought in people from Sandzak and Albanians to Bijeljina in preparation for the blockade of Bijeljina and the war against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who Djuk Smail is?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not good at remembering names. I don't even know my children's names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know your children's names?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Mr. May, as you have cautioned me and said that I asked improper questions, there are some other questions which in your opinion could be -- have been along these lines, but the witness himself says he doesn't know the names of his children, and the improper questions that I asked are relevant in order to assess the credibility of this person's testimony, a person who was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think he means that literally he doesn't remember his children's names or whether he forgets them from time to time. It's a common enough experience for anybody. If you want to raise something along these lines, we better go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. Let's move into private session just for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The two matters are these: Mr. Nice, on Exhibit 414, we did not exhibit tab 2, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And we should remove that then from our bundles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And Mr. Milosevic, you want to exhibit your Reuters report; is that right? Very well. Could you hand it in, please, and we'll get a number for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. We're going to get a number for the Reuters report.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Reuters report will be Defence Exhibit 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, do you know a company called Djuk Auto in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djuk Auto did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Djuk Auto. It had premises, large premises. Obrijez. You know where Obrijez is, I presume.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it had large office premises there at Obrijez, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that that is where the Green Berets and Patriotic League had their camp? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. And do you happen to know some people who were -- had nicknames Sajto and Gara?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know them. Well, then, you ought to know that it is precisely those people that conducted the training in that particular camp.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the guys, but I didn't know that they did any training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they are from the Silosi settlement, district; right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't know about the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do know the men?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know nothing of their activities.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know nothing about either the Red -- Green Berets or the Patriotic League that were trained there at that camp at Obrijez? You know nothing about that, is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Just tell me this: When you set out towards the Srbija cafe, were there any incidents that took place before that, any incident before that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bomb was thrown at the Istanbul cafe. That was enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that bomb was thrown at the Cafe Istanbul.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And uniformed persons were being collected up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the bomb at the Istanbul thrown before?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A day or two before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to you one day, although here in the statement you say two days, and my information tells me that it was about ten days before, but immediately before you set out on that particular day to throw a bomb, nothing was actually going on, nothing was happening; right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean "nothing"? How can you say "nothing"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what was going on then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army was amassing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What army?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An attack on Bijeljina was being organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An attack on Bijeljina was being organised from the Srbija cafe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An attack on Bijeljina, you say?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. The -- Seselj's men, Arkan's men, and Mirko's men, and all the others were collecting up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that they attacked Bijeljina before you threw the bomb?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were preparing to attack Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was in the Srbija cafe. I first went there, then I went back, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But nobody had attacked anybody before that; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody attacked but they were thinking about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You thought that people were preparing an attack; right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they threw a bomb at the Cafe Istanbul, and that happened before. Was that enough? Wasn't that enough? And after that they began to rally their ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that man was arrested and taken off to Tuzla, and this person was not -- was mentally incompetent and he was taken to prison, and the bomb was thrown at Croats and Serbs. Are you saying that the Muslim forces had not blocked Bijeljina prior to that, before the conflict in Bijeljina actually broke out? There was no blockade of Bijeljina, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's dealt with that question. Now, this is all repetition about the questions on the cafe. You've dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. As you went to hospital, was there a Muslim barricade set up by the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago you said there was no blockade.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims held control of the hospital when I was there the first two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But when you set off to hospital, there was a Muslim barricade erected there; right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand you -- I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a Muslim barricade at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later on. There were predominantly Muslims by the hospital and the settlements around were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know anybody up at the barricade? Is it true that it was by Redzep's house or, rather, between the mosque and Redzep's house, the location of the barricade?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. I was injured and I was going to hospital and there was nobody there then. And during the two or three days that I spent there, they did hold the hospital, and that was sufficient time for me to recuperate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, during those three days, you didn't see the barricade there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was lying in bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when did you see a Muslim barricade then if you say that during the first three days you didn't see one?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not barricades, sir. What I saw was that the Muslims were holding the hospital and that area for two or three days. I don't know exactly how long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just show you a picture. I'm not going to take up too much more of your time. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem to be in this set. Ah, here it is. Just when I thought it was missing. Is this -- take a look at this picture and tell me if this is the Muslim barricade set up at Redzep's house or, rather, the machine-gun nest. Just that photograph with the sandbags. Could it be placed onto the ELMO. Is that it? Is that what you saw?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I see it when I said I hadn't seen it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you told me that there was a barricade next to the hospital at one point.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I said that the Muslims held the hospital for two or three days. I didn't see any barricades, you see. But of course there were barricades. It's normal. It's normal that there were barricades later on, I assume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's normal but you didn't see them. I see, you didn't see them. And you don't recognise this barricade at Redzep's house?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I recognise it when I didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Please let me have that picture back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the picture has never been displayed. May I just have a look at it before it goes back to the accused?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Show it to the Prosecution, please, and then back to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, are you all right? Are you okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've got, at the most, another quarter of an hour, if you need it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me try to use those 15 minutes, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Dr. Kicanovic, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a doctor from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, when this was happening Dr. Kicanovic was not even in Bijeljina, never mind in the hospital. Is that incorrect, what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it's incorrect when the man treated me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe Dr. Kicanovic for me? What does he look like?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An older man. An older man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, please describe him.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grey hair, maybe between 55 and 60. I don't know exactly. I may be wrong. Looking fit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much shorter than you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little shorter than me. A little. Not much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned Andrija Tufekcic, a Croat from Brcko, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that is not true, that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who? Who was killed?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tufekcic.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with me in Doboj. That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. It's not true. Very well, well, when was he exchanged?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was exchanged before you.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among those first five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Now, let's look into your explanation that the Serbs were planning an attack on Bijeljina. Did you see any kind of an attack on Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any kind of attack?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see an attack on Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the shooting in front of the Srbija coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But who planned the attack on Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko, the radicals, and Arkan's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I not know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not a good answer. How did you know? You didn't attend their meetings. How do you know that they were planning an attack on Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What were armed soldiers doing walking around Bijeljina? What for?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But very well. From the Istanbul coffee bar, was fire opened on Serbs who were in the Srbija coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Serbs started shooting, then they responded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your incident, yes. So do you consider your wounding in the leg to be an attack by the Serbian side?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never stopped shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember that the Muslims were carrying weapons from the mosque and by the evening they had already taken control of the city? Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember that weapons in the SDA premises, the Party of Democratic Action, were being distributed by Alija Saracevic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that true or not? Say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember sniper nests on the water tower, the silo, at Zitopromet when Stojan Stojanovic was wounded?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could I remember when I was in hospital?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. But that day, before you went to hospital, do you remember harassing the guests at the Semberka Grill Restaurant owned by Ljubisa Rosic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember. Well, do you remember that you were harassing all the Serbs walking along Marsal Tito Street?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only Serbs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember that either?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that this attack and the blockade of Bijeljina had spoiled Izetbegovic's plan to capture all locations in Bosnia-Herzegovina at once, and you were in a hurry. You hastened. You did that too quickly, and you spoiled the plan.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Alija Izetbegovic addressed a call to the JNA then, an appeal for the JNA to prevent the conflict, and they came to prevent it?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the Plavsic woman said too, that the JNA would resolve everything, and it did indeed at the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did they come to prevent the conflict? I wasn't there so I don't know. Alija Izetbegovic asked the JNA to prevent conflicts in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To come and kill people. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did the JNA come?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did they prevent the conflict?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they prevented it. They killed people. And Arkan's men and the Seselj's men went on looting and taking the booty to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're claiming the JNA came to kill Muslims and to loot?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. From the garrison. Yes. They were based there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that night just when the Muslims attacked and blocked Muslims and captured the centre of the city, the hospital, the Municipal Assembly, the electricity board and other buildings before the Serbs reacted in any way whatsoever? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that that same night, on the 31st of March, the warehouse of the barracks was broken into and weapons distributed publicly to the Muslims? Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a bare-faced lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know that in the park a bunker was formed, as in other places in the town? I showed you one of those a moment ago. Very well, then. Is it clear that that is what provoked the beginning of the war and not any attack by Serbs? Is that true or not, Mr. Gusalic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not true. That's not how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you are not aware of the snipers from the silo or from the bunkers or the barricades and the fact that Bijeljina was taken control of and completely blocked before the Serbs reacted at all? So you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you have got five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that this operation, that is the attack on the Serbs in Bijeljina, was led by Hasan Piric, who was later killed? Had you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that a unit called the Black Swans bore his name because he founded that unit, he set it up?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasan Siric maybe, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That man did not get killed. He's alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he set up the Black Swans unit that was called after him?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can you say when the Muslim forces took control of the city? When exactly did that happen? When did the Muslim forces take control of the city?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't know how long we're going on with this. You've got two minutes more. Did the Muslims at any stage take control of the city? Can you help us with that, Mr. Gusalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the whole city. For example, the hospital was controlled by the Muslims maybe for two to three days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Can you help us as to when that was or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 31st, up until perhaps the 2nd, 3rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Of what month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] April, March/April.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. What the Muslim forces had captured and blocked in Bijeljina, when did that happen? Just tell me when, on what day.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded on the 31st, around 8.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it then that the Muslims blocked Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to say. I don't know when they blocked it. I was in hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that in the settlement called Vozderic, the Muslims had some conflicts among themselves and there were some casualties?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't heard of that. I hear it from you now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, then, how many weapons did the Muslims in Bijeljina have when they blocked the town regardless whether they blocked the whole town or part of it? You say that you know about the hospital and nothing more. I showed you one machine-gun nest which is of course not in the hospital. So how much weapons did the Muslims have then?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There were some hunting rifles. Mostly hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how many?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number. A small number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And are you aware of the fact that after the situation was settled and calmed in the town of Bijeljina - and when I say Bijeljina, I mean the town of Bijeljina - that the Muslims surrendered more than 500 long-barrelled weapons, which means more than 500 rifles and automatic rifles, and that some had fled with weapons, but over 500 were surrendered when the situation calmed down? You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One more question, Mr. Milosevic, and then your time is up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me then, since you're claiming in answer to my question as to whether you knew that Alija Izetbegovic had asked the JNA to calm the situation down, when did you see the JNA in Bijeljina? Or, rather, to make my question shorter, during those conflicts which flared up in Bijeljina, was the JNA present at all in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mrs. Plavsic, she said that. And I think she made sure that they should come to their assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not -- leave Plavsic alone. I'll have occasion to ask her questions. My question, Mr. Gusalic, is in those clashes on the 31st of March, the 1st and 2nd of April, did members of the JNA participate in any way?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. In the attack on Bijeljina, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the members of the JNA attack Bijeljina from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In collaboration with local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said where did they attack Bijeljina from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From across the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they crossed the Drina, JNA members, and attacked Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've had your time. Mr. Tapuskovic, have you any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have some questions, Your Honour, for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will adjourn now. Twenty minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Possibly hopefully before Mr. Tapuskovic asks questions, with the Special Rapporteur's report, it's now available for you. It's not a particularly thick document, as you can see. However, there are two points. First of all, by reading the entries at the back of the document, it would appear that the visits to Batkovic camp were on the 17th of October, 1992. The second point is this: The accused was only provided with two pages because those were the only two pages that were Rule 68, in our judgement and, therefore, those went his way, and they contain not only comments on Batkovic but also material on other topics of interest to the Chamber and which I suppose I could technically adduce in re-examination if I wanted to. But the balance of the document also contains opinions, some of which are by no means favourable to the interests that the accused of course seeks to advance and therefore the Chamber might want to exercise caution before deciding whether to mark the whole document as an exhibit or to mark it for identification or something of that sort.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, may I just ask one more question. I have several, but just one, because it relates to his statements, and I think it is important. It won't take more than one minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusalic, is it true that in the period we are talking about, you appeared on Bijeljina television and also in Trnovo. You gave an interview to a foreign TV station, and that in both statements you said that the Muslims were to blame for the war, that you were treated correctly, that you had mistreated the Serbs and so on? Is this true? I am referring to two of your interviews, on Bijeljina television and a foreign TV station in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me to say that but I didn't say that. How could I say something that was not true?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say that or not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm saying that you said.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. No, that's why they beat me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there are no such statements of yours?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. They don't exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've really had your time, and if you want to ask questions like that, you should -- just a moment. Mr. Gusalic, please. We're not going to go on with this. The witness has answered. If there are other matters to clear up, the Prosecution can do so in re-examination. Right. We're going to adjourn now. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, along with the statement of Mr. Gusalic which he gave to the investigators of the Tribunal on the 11th and 12th of March, 1997, pursuant to Article 66, another of his statements was presented, one which he gave on the 27th of November, 1993, at the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the centre for security, the sector for state security of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As I say, that was on the 27th of November, 1993. And it was provided pursuant to Rule 66. Questioned by Mr. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gusalic, you spoke today during the examination-in-chief about what you saw, as you yourself say, in Smajne Vode, when in a truck -- when you loaded into a truck, as you yourself said, 40 civilians who had lost their lives in the way that you described.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svjetlice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svjetlice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said 40.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Svjetlice. At Smajne Vode we dug trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ah, so you mean the place was different. Right. I apologise. My mistake. How do you explain or, rather, can you explain to the Court - not to take up too much time, let me ask you directly - that in your statement dated the 27th of November, 1993, that is to say very soon after the events at the material time, you make no mention of that, about what you testified today during the examination-in-chief. You didn't mention it then either.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, lots of things were happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But this is an event which would merit being stated first if you did indeed see something and if this was done. Can you explain why in that 1993 statement of yours you didn't mention it the way you did today? Can you or can you not?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that first statement, I make no mention of the sexual abuses either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's precisely what I wanted to ask you. That was my second question. Why at that time nor on the 11th and 12th of March, 1997, did you make no mention of the sexual abuse to which you were exposed? That's precisely what I wanted to ask you. Can you explain that to us? You didn't say it in 1993, and you didn't say it to the Tribunal's investigators either. Can you explain that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, sir, I can explain it. I think it was the shame. I think it's a shame -- it's shameful to talk about those things, but finally I came to realise that it wasn't my shame, it was shame on the people who did it and shame on the people who issued orders to that effect. It is their shame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I can understand that. But how can you explain not having mentioned such a terrible thing that happened to you if you truly did see the victims that you talk about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: He's explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And one more question referring to what you said in your statement of the 11th March. You said that you were taken out of the camp, and you went to do trench digging, and you say to the investigators: "We had to dig trenches up at the front but not during the shooting." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you explain to the Trial Chamber the following: You said that there were three persons wounded, three prisoners wounded who had been injured. How were they wounded and injured if there was no shooting while you were trench digging? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day we were digging the trenches, the Serbs started shooting, but a grenade fell, a shell fell. We were divided up into groups, and a shell fell and that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in other words, what you told the investigators is not correct, that you had to, you were forced to dig trenches but there was no shooting. So there was shooting, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few more questions, Mr. Gusalic. And on the topic of statements, you've been asked questions about two of them, or -- two of them. The one provided to the Ministry of Internal Affairs in Tuzla was actually dated the 27th, not the 17th of November, 1993. Can you remember now if that was read over to you after you prepared it, whether you checked it for accuracy?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that statement, there's a reference that wasn't drawn to your attention, to the following: When you were at Batkovic camp, it says you were taken off to do forced labour. You had to fetch and carry different loads, and you were taken to do trench digging at Svjetlice, Smajne Vode and Predujevo. Your statement then goes on to say that you were taken to the frontline to carry away the bodies of Chetniks who had been killed and that you were forced to dig up your own dead fighters and to replace them with the bodies of Chetniks. Now, that's not something you've covered in your evidence today. Do you remember saying those things to those investigators in 1993? Carrying away the bodies of Chetniks who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And digging up your own dead fighters --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was not in Batkovic, that was in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And digging up your own dead fighters and replacing them with the bodies of Chetniks. Was that something that happened?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also in this statement mention being forced to eat hay while you were imprisoned in Batkovic, being forced to do that by Zoko and Major [phoen] as you've described them to be. Was that true? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's of course entirely a matter for the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, had it been hay, that wouldn't have been a bad thing. This was straw, because straw is sharp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's entirely a matter for the Chamber whether, in light of the cross-examination and what the witness says both about his reading of the statements or having them read to him whether the Chamber wants them exhibited. It would appear that there is no evidence from the witness that the statements contain anything that is false. It appears indeed that they contain material that is accurate, and the only question is whether the omission of the particular passage is of significance. They will be available should the Chamber decide it wants them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will consider that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the topic of the statements, perhaps the last question, the finding of the Muslim bodies that had been slaughtered it appears is not in either of these statements, that is either the one made in 1993 or the one made to the ICTY later. Do you remember discussing that when you came here in the last few days, in fact a couple of weeks, in preparation of giving your evidence? Do you remember discussing the finding of those dead Muslim bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did discuss that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The accused is suggesting to you I think in some way that because it's not in your statement you've made it up and it's not true. Is it true? Did it happen?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did happen, and there are other witnesses, people who were with me when we loaded it up, loaded them up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a few more questions, Mr. Gusalic, then. You don't want to identify the particular person who took you to hospital after the grenade. Just answer this question, please, if you will: Were you taken to the hospital by somebody whom you knew? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in some way a friend of yours? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a close friend but an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it because you know him and you would be giving his identity that you don't want to name him in this court? Is that the reason?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's a family man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've been asked questions by the accused about who was in the cafe before you rode there on your horse with the grenade. How long before you went with the grenade had you been in that cafe yourself?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My mistake entirely. How many minutes before you went with the grenade, or how many hours or how many days before you went with the grenade had you been in the cafe to see who was there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not long. Not much time went by. Perhaps an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were last in the cafe, were there any Muslims there?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Srbija cafe, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've spoken --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least I couldn't notice any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke of how Muslims were compelled to fight because of threats that would be made to their families left at home. Is this something that you experienced yourself or that you were simply told of by other people?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have occasion to experience it myself. I was in the camp. But my brothers did. Two of my brothers experienced it. They went to the -- for the Republika Srpska, and their family stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of this happening to any other families, and if so, give us an idea, if you can, how many other such families told you of this.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the majority of Muslims who went to war for the Serb republic, for the Republika Srpska, had threats against them mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked a question about whether there was a detention centre at Popovi as opposed to Amajlije. The Chamber can see both those towns or villages marked on page 29 immediately to the east of Bijeljina. Do you know both those villages, Popovi and Amajlije?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do they lie --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know them very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do they lie on the same road? It's not clear from our map, but do they lie on the same road that turns off the road that would cross over to Serbia at Badovinci?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA GUSALIC [Resumed]
